other_failure_modes.name: Cross-validation leakage during feature engineering
other_failure_modes.description: Features that depend on the distribution of the dataset (such as frequency encoding, cross-entity diversity/nunique features, and median imputation) are computed on the entire training dataset before cross-validation splitting. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the CV scores overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: Failure to drop high-cardinality raw date columns
other_failure_modes.description: After extracting useful numerical features (year, month, day, etc.) from date columns, the agent fails to drop the original date strings. These are subsequently treated as categorical features, leading to massive cardinality, memory waste, and potential overfitting in models.

other_failure_modes.name: Failure to log-transform highly skewed target for training
other_failure_modes.description: The target variable (e.g., 'Amount in USD') is likely highly right-skewed. While the agent creates a log-transformed version for fold stratification, it trains the models (including neural networks with MSE loss) directly on the raw target scale, making them overly sensitive to extreme outliers.

summary: The agent provides a sophisticated solution with deep learning, gradient boosting, and optimized ensembling. However, it computes several distribution-dependent features (like frequency encoding and median imputation) on the full training set before CV splitting, causing validation leakage. Additionally, it fails to drop raw date columns after extracting date components, leading to unnecessary high-cardinality categorical features, and trains directly on a highly skewed raw target instead of a log-transformed version.
